answer: One applicant catalogues relics at a mountain haven archive for 60 days. Each morning the cataloguer counts open blooms on the courtyard lotus pond, then files one dated page on one relic, weight, stamp, and shelf. A warden signs the page that day and matches the bloom count, so a copied page fails by evening. One missed day restarts the 60 days, and a forged page voids the 500 token bond. So faking 10,000 identities needs 600,000 signed mornings and 5,000,000 frozen tokens. The catalogue is a wall raised brick by brick in daylight, and a thief would have to rebuild it the same slow way.
